question: Does Fowler's 1918 Philippine fish list provide a species record, collection context, or evidence for an introduction date relevant to the later Monopterus claims?

primaryArticlePage.title: A List of Philippine Fishes
primaryArticlePage.author: Henry W. Fowler
primaryArticlePage.accessStatus: JSTOR labels the item FREE and says it is openly available as part of an Open JSTOR Collection.
primaryArticlePage.copyrightNote: JSTOR states that, to its knowledge, the journal issue is in the public domain and may be used accordingly, while disclaiming representation or warranty. No independent legal determination was made.

retrievalAssessment.whatWasReviewed: The JSTOR article landing-page metadata and terms note were readable.
retrievalAssessment.whatWasNotReviewed: The four original article pages, including page 62, were not retrieved or visually read in this environment; no species entry, introduction statement, locality, specimen label, collection date, or citation within Fowler is confirmed here.
retrievalAssessment.secondaryCrossReference: FishBase's Monopterus albus reference list separately maps Fowler 1918 to the historical name Fluta alba on page 62. That secondary index is a lead for checking the primary page, not a substitute for reading it.
retrievalAssessment.bibliographyCrossReference: The NFRDI-hosted bibliography of Philippine fishes independently lists the same Fowler citation and pages 62–65.

evidenceLimits.dateInterpretation: A 1918 publication or list entry does not establish when any fish was introduced, first arrived, or was collected.
evidenceLimits.taxonomicIdentity: The historical name Fluta alba and later Monopterus albus usage do not by themselves identify the modern taxon of the referenced specimen or population.
evidenceLimits.localityAndSpecimens: No Pasig or NCR locality, collection date, catalog number, accession number, or specimen determination is established by the landing page or secondary cross-reference.

evidenceDecision.decision: Update the source record with JSTOR's open article page and public-domain note, but retain Fowler as a primary-page review lead. Keep the 1918 publication year separate from any introduction-year claim.

nextActions: Open the JSTOR stable article page in a normal browser and review page 62 plus any surrounding note if access permits; record only Fowler's verbatim historical name and directly stated source context.

If Fowler supplies no collection or provenance details, keep the item as a historical inventory entry and continue to the reported Smithsonian lot reclassification without treating the list year as an introduction year.
Seek the catalog/accession identifiers behind the reported 14-lot reclassification; do not infer Fowler's specimens are among those lots without a matching identifier.
